item.title: Norse mythology art by IrenHorrors
item.description:
The goddess Sif had fair hair that Loki once cut off. To avoid the wrath of Thor, her husband, Loki acquired valuable items for the gods; so Sif got hair of gold and Thor got his hammer Mjölnir
The three children of the jötnar Loki and Angrboda: the great wolf Fenrir, Hel the ruler of the realm of the dead, and the world serpent Jörmungandr. Jötnar is often translated as ’giants’ but had all shapes and sizes
The golden apples of Idunn kept the gods young. Once Idunn was kidnapped by a jötunn named Thjazi; the gods then aged and weakened until she was returned
Skadi was the daughter of Thjazi but became a goddess of Asgard. She was associated with winter, ski hunting and mountains. On her, see https://imgur.com/gallery/uWRuTWU
In Northern European myths the Wild Hunt heralds catastrophes such as war or plague, and it could abduct people. In Scandinavian legends it was headed by Odin
The cunning Loki was the friend, or sworn blood-brother, of Odin but would end up a foe of Asgard
Freyja is best known as a goddess of love, sex, fertility and wealth but was also associated with magic, war and death. On the latter, see https://imgur.com/gallery/3sKGYee
Freya had a wagon drawn by cats as well as the boar mount Hildisvíni (“battle swine”)
The three female Norns named Urd, Verdandi and Skuld wove the destiny of gods and men
The loyal Sigyn by the side of her husband Loki, during his punishment for causing the death of the god Balder. On his captivity, see https://imgur.com/gallery/3LEkJCC Credits: IrenHorrors https://www.deviantart.com/irenhorrors/gallery https://www.instagram.com/irenhorrors/
